headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risks from document OCR feeding a chat bot; no direct shared-channel evidence, so pairwise risk is inferred.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: PaddleOCR ingests documents/images and can run browsers, while Rasa consumes conversational text over messaging APIs. If OCR output is forwarded into Rasa without sanitization, attacker-controlled document text can become instructions. No shared channel is documented, so this is inferred rather than observed.
conditions: IF OCR output is copied into Rasa training or runtime messages without filtering
IF a document contains instruction-like text that Rasa treats as dialogue content
mitigations: Add a strict content separator between OCR text and bot instructions
Strip or escape prompt-like markers before handing OCR output to Rasa
Review a sample OCR-to-bot path with adversarial documents
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all OCR-derived text
requires-engineering: enforce allowlisted message schemas between systems

B_data_leakage.rationale: PaddleOCR touches documents and images, and Rasa handles text and voice. Both show allowlisted egress and no secrets/OAuth scopes, so a direct leakage path is not evident. The main risk is accidental sharing of document contents into chat channels, which is limited unless the operator bridges them.
conditions: IF document contents are forwarded from PaddleOCR into a public or external Rasa channel
IF the operator routes sensitive OCR output into Twilio or messaging integrations
mitigations: Keep OCR outputs in a private workspace
Disable external chat connectors for sensitive runs
Redact PII before sending text to Rasa
requires-engineering: add per-field data-loss prevention
requires-engineering: segregate sensitive OCR jobs from customer-support bots

C_capability_conflict.rationale: PaddleOCR has API-call surfaces and browser execution, while Rasa exposes multiple messaging APIs but does not support multiple instances. There is no evidence of shared writable state or overlapping mutable resources, so conflict is possible only if the operator wires both to the same backend or queue.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same downstream queue or database
IF the operator shares a mutable workspace between OCR and chatbot workflows
mitigations: Assign separate queues or databases
Run the agents under distinct service accounts
Avoid shared writable directories
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared state
requires-engineering: introduce optimistic concurrency checks

D_cascading_error.rationale: PaddleOCR can produce extracted text that Rasa may ingest as dialogue content. Because Rasa is a customer-support bot framework, it may act on or surface that text without independent verification. The pairwise pathway exists in default integration patterns, though the exact bridge is undocumented.
conditions: IF OCR output is used as an input message or knowledge snippet for Rasa
IF Rasa responses are generated from OCR text without a verification step
mitigations: Insert a human review step for high-stakes OCR text
Mark OCR-derived content as untrusted in the bot pipeline
Test with malformed and adversarial documents
requires-engineering: add citation/provenance checks before bot responses
requires-engineering: block autonomous actions from OCR-derived inputs

E_compliance.rationale: PaddleOCR processes documents and images, while Rasa handles text and voice through external messaging APIs. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in either profile, so compliance risk is limited to operator-chosen data flows such as sending regulated document text into chat channels.
conditions: IF regulated document data is routed from PaddleOCR into external messaging integrations
IF the deployment stores OCR transcripts longer than the source-document policy allows
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to external chat connectors
Set short retention on OCR transcripts
Document the data flow for compliance review
requires-engineering: map residency and retention controls end to end
requires-engineering: add deletion/export handling for OCR-derived records
